> Over a small finite field, where $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2$, **what is `DivFamZar` supposed to be?**

Certifiability needs two $k$-rational points of $\mathbb{P}^1$ off the support's image at every base point. `Challenge.lean:96-99` states the Jacobian over an ARBITRARY field, and nothing in `Picard/` or `RiemannRoch/` assumes more than `[Field k]`. - **(b)** plan a descent lane — `divQProj` (`Picard/DivSchemeQProj.lean`) is the right lever for fpqc descent from a big enough $k'/k$;

## 1. THE STANDING QUESTION FOR THE HUMAN — OPEN, UNCHANGED, AND THE ONLY OPEN PART

> Over a small finite field, where $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)| = q + 1 < n + 2$, **what is `DivFamZar` supposed to be?**

Certifiability needs two $k$-rational points of $\mathbb{P}^1$ off the support's image at every base point. `Challenge.lean:96-99` states the Jacobian over an ARBITRARY field, and nothing in `Picard/` or `RiemannRoch/` assumes more than `[Field k]`. - **(a)** accept $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)| \ge n + 2$ as a hypothesis, and record that the challenge as stated is then not solved for small $q$;
- **(b)** plan a descent lane — `divQProj` (`Picard/DivSchemeQProj.lean`) is the right lever for fpqc descent from a big enough $k'/k$;
- **(c)** generalize the pinned charts to closed points of degree $d \ge 2$, paying `Gamma(P1 k, chartOpen k i) ≃ Polynomial k` (`Curve/P1Charts.lean:234,239`) and `isPrincipalIdealRing_chartSections` (`Curve/P1Points.lean:64`), since $\mathrm{Cl}(\mathbb{P}^1 \setminus \{\text{degree-}d\text{ point}\}) = \mathbb{Z}/d$.

It should be settled BEFORE anyone builds the $\mathrm{GL}_2(k)$ action on $\mathbb{P}^1$ (leaf `p1-aut`, still `pending`) — it decides whether that work is worth doing at all.

## 2. THE MATHEMATICAL HALF — ANSWERED, sharp, no longer yours

`informal/spec-dd-r.md` ADDENDUM 4 §4.4 answers the quantitative question in both directions, and the bound guessed originally is now known to be **sharp**: the pinned-pair route R1 works precisely when $|\mathbb{P}^1(k)| \ge g+2$, and fails exactly when $\sum_{c \in \mathbb{P}^1(k)} e_c \le n$ (with $e_c$ the minimal degree of a closed point of $C$ over $c$), where one can place $\xi_s$ so that $s \in W_c$ for **every** $c$ and no pinned pair confines. Roadmap leaf `...ddr.certificate.field-size` is `done`. **This half needs no human input** — it does not change the design question in §1, which is about what the object should BE, not about where the bound sits.

## 3. THE "CHEAPER OPTION" — REFUTED (2026-07-26, run 0048 round 2)

REFUTED: *"relaxing just the chart-wise partitions to a joint covering drops the requirement from two avoided points to ONE. Worth trying before anyone builds PGL_2."* It buys nothing, and the reason is a typing fact, not a failed proof. `FinCoverData` types its pieces INTO the charts — `h0 : Fin m0 -> Gamma(relCurve, V0)` (`DivisorFamily.lean:166`), `h1` into `V1` (`:168`), `pieces := Sum.elim (basicOpen . h0) (basicOpen . h1)` (`:186`) — so every piece is a basic open of one of the two PINNED charts by construction, whatever the partition data says. Per-piece swallow-or-miss already holds for any cover by opens (`DivSchemeCertZarConn.lean:98` uses only openness), so a connected divisor still lands in one piece, and `basicOpen_le` puts that piece inside one chart. Changing the partition FIELDS cannot change where the pieces LIVE. Recorded as roadmap leaf `...ddr.certificate.joint-cover`, status `rejected`, with the 10-file rebuild cost if anyone tries it anyway.

The sharp form to quote from now on: **NO repair that keeps the pieces inside the preimages of a FIXED PAIR of points of $\mathbb{P}^1$ can work.** Only R1 (vary the pinned pair — needs $\mathrm{Aut}(\mathbb{P}^1)$) or R2 (generalize the piece type) remain.

## 4. THE ORIGINAL CORRECTION TO I-0333 — historical record

CORRECTION TO MY ANSWER ON I-0333, filed in the same round after an adversarial pass. The POSITIVE half — "the repair is cheap and it is not a decision" — was too optimistic in three ways, and one of them put the DIFFERENT question of §1 back to you.

The $Z(\diamond)$ chart does not confine its divisors; the counterexample is real; the obstruction is `DivEq`-invariant and therefore bites `DivFamZar` itself; confinement is an open condition on the base, so an atlas may legitimately record avoidance. 3. The diagnosis "the binding constraint is `FinCoverData`" was too narrow. Per-piece swallow-or-miss follows from (c1)-finiteness for ANY cover by opens; only the chart-wise partitions of unity upgrade "inside one piece" to "inside one chart".
